exposure: Type of cesarean section (emergency vs. planned)
cohort: 253 mothers of children/adolescents (2-15 years old) diagnosed with ASD and 852 mothers of children/adolescents in the control group in northern Minas Gerais state, Brazil
finding: The presence of meconium-stained amniotic fluid, delivery by cesarean section, and exposure to two or more unfavorable peripartum events were associated with an increased likelihood of ASD development in children and adolescents.
mod_finding: Both cesarean delivery in general and emergency cesarean section specifically were associated with an increased likelihood of ASD development.
